chunks.heading: Coming back from injury
chunks.content:
## Coming back from injury

Tore my ACL and went through surgery. The recovery period meant weeks of not being able to do the thing I loved most, which taught me a level of patience I didn't have before, showing up for slow, unglamorous physical therapy work with no immediate payoff. Getting back to playing sports afterward was less about physical recovery and more about not giving up on something after a real setback. It's the same mindset I bring to a hard technical problem: staying with it past the point where quitting would be easier.

## CRMN internship, Sousse (06/2026 to 08/2026)

Centre de Recherche en Microélectronique et Nanotechnologie. Official title: "Contextual Agentic Reasoning via RAG and Interoperability APIs in Home-Monitoring Frameworks." Worked on a real-time home health-monitoring system with a two-tier architecture connected only through a Kafka message broker (Tier 1: fast, rule-based; Tier 2: slower, AI reasoning-based).

Aziz worked on contextual agentic reasoning for Tier 2 (choosing the orchestration framework, then extending the pipeline to reason over enriched context across multiple scenarios), and on the RAG retrieval stack and interoperability services connecting the tiers. Benchmarked four vector databases and several orchestration frameworks for latency, reliability, and scalability before integrating the best combination. Stack: RAG, ChromaDB, FAISS, Qdrant, Llama, Kafka, Docker, LangGraph, CrewAI, RAGAS, Git, Python.

The internship is finished. He is now continuing this work with his supervisor toward a research publication, and it gave him a genuine interest in agentic AI research.

chunks.heading: Agentic orchestration framework benchmark
chunks.content:
## Agentic orchestration framework benchmark

Comparative benchmarking study of agentic AI orchestration frameworks: LangGraph, CrewAI, AG2/AutoGen, and the OpenAI Agents SDK.

Built a minimal two-agent sequential pipeline as a consistent test harness across all frameworks, using a local Ollama model (qwen2.5:7b) so the comparison was not affected by different model quality. Used separate virtual environments per framework to avoid dependency conflicts.

chunks.heading: Contextual agentic reasoning for home health monitoring
chunks.content:
## Contextual agentic reasoning for home health monitoring

Built during the CRMN internship (Sousse, 06/2026 to 08/2026). Official title: "Contextual Agentic Reasoning via RAG and Interoperability APIs in Home-Monitoring Frameworks."

A system that monitors a patient's vital signs at home, decides whether an alert is needed, and determines what kind of network support the situation requires. Two tiers, connected only through a Kafka message broker: Tier 1 is fast and rule-based, Tier 2 is slower and reasoning-based.

Aziz worked on: choosing the orchestration framework for Tier 2, then extending the Tier 2 pipeline to reason over enriched context across multiple emergency scenarios, plus the RAG retrieval stack and the interoperability services connecting the two tiers (a retrieval service and a network-request emission service).

Benchmarked four vector databases (ChromaDB, FAISS, Qdrant, and a fourth) and several orchestration frameworks for latency, reliability, and scalability, then integrated the best combination. Stack: Llama, Kafka, Docker, LangGraph, CrewAI, RAGAS, Git, Python.

All data used was synthetic, since no real smart-home hardware was available.

**Status:** internship complete. He is now continuing this work with his supervisor toward a research publication, this is what gave him a genuine interest in agentic AI research.

## Subject 4: Intelligent Application with Spring AI & LLM

Internship/academic backend project. Spring Boot 3.x on Java 21, with REST APIs, conversational memory, and AI-assisted content generation.

**Architecture decisions:** UUID primary keys, TEXT over VARCHAR for message content, Flyway over Hibernate auto-DDL for schema management, Ollama instead of a paid API as the LLM provider. chunks.heading: StockCare, healthcare AI hackathon
chunks.content:
## StockCare, healthcare AI hackathon

Project name: StockCare (Predictive Demand and Priority-Aware Distribution Network). Team name: Team Chaneb+.

Three-layer architecture: Layer 1 does pharmacy-level demand forecasting, Layer 2 is a depot-side priority classification engine, Layer 3 does routing with mixed-integer linear programming (MILP).

Aziz is responsible for Layer 2, and implemented a reinforcement learning agent with adaptive weighting for prioritization, defining the state and action space and the reward function himself.

Uses the official Tunisian AMM (market authorization) database from the DPM (dpm.tn), covering 6,058 active drug authorizations, to ground the forecasting in real regulatory data.

**Status:** phase 1 (problem/solution write-up) was submitted. This is a hackathon entry, not a finished product, and no final placement is confirmed yet. Present it as an in-progress hackathon project, not as a completed result.

chunks.heading: Technical skills, grouped by area
chunks.content:
## Technical skills, grouped by area

These are drawn from Aziz's actual projects and internships, not a self-rated list.

**AI and machine learning:** deep reinforcement learning (including CVaR risk-aware formulations), computer vision (YOLOv8, OpenCV, MobileNet), sentiment analysis (DistilBERT), Graph Neural Networks, agentic orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, evaluated AG2/AutoGen and OpenAI Agents SDK), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with ChromaDB, FAISS and Qdrant, RAG evaluation with RAGAS, local model serving with Ollama, Microsoft Agent Framework, XGBoost, Kaggle competitions.

**Backend and systems:** Java (Spring Boot 3.x on Java 21, J2EE), Python (FastAPI, Flask), REST API design, JPA, Flyway migrations, PostgreSQL, H2, Kafka as a message broker between decoupled services, Docker, Node-RED, MQTT.

**Frontend and mobile:** React, Mapbox GL JS, Flutter.

**Data and infrastructure:** US Census ACS data, H3 hexagonal spatial grids, Firebase (Auth and Firestore), Raspberry Pi and IoT sensor pipelines, Arduino.

**Other technical work:** Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) solvers, semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations, portfolio optimization (mean-variance, chance-constrained, kurtosis-based).

**Languages used day to day:** Python, Java. French and English both used for technical work (see profile.md for language proficiency).
